newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's good weather to keep harvest on track.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's good weather to keep harvest on track.

text.p: Decent weather so far means Ukraine could reach its grain harvest target of 35 million tonnes, well above last year's disastrous 25.4 million, Western experts and traders said on Monday.

"Things do look quite good," said Stephan von Cramon Taubadel, an agricultural economist with the German Advisory Group on Economic Reforms of Ukraine. Looking at 35 million tonnes and the weather conditions, "the forecasts seem reasonable at the moment."
A Western trader said official predictions would likely be fulfilled.
"They've said 20 million tonnes in winter wheat and there will be two to three million tonnes in sunseeds," he said.
The Agriculture Ministry's output forecast includes about 20 million tonnes of winter wheat, spring wheat, barley and maize (corn) -- higher than last year's drought-hit harvest.
Bohdan Chomiak, representative with U.S.-based Chemonics, which is working to promote reform in the largely state-controlled farm sector said "It's really a question of the weather."
Taubadel said winter wheat had done well this year compared to last year, when the crop totalled a puny 13.4 million tonnes.
"Most of the (winter wheat) crop came through in good condition," he said. But low input levels meant final output was at the mercy of the weather.
"They'll always have 26 to 35 million tonnes," he said. "It depends on what the weather does to them."

Ukraine's cash-strapped agriculture sector has had little money for seeds, herbicides, pesticides, fuel and machinery since breaking free of the Soviet Union nearly six years ago. The former breadbasket once produced bumper harvests of 50 million tonnes and more but has seen output plummet as it struggles through market economy reforms.
Western grain traders said they often had to finance deals by providing inputs in exchange for grain delivered later.
The government has forecast grain exports of six million tonnes from this year's harvest.
Ukraine completed sowing 13.51 million hectares to spring grain, up from last year's 13.12 million. Private farmers planted 4.66 million hectares with spring grain.
It sowed 6.36 million hectares with winter wheat, 700,000 with winter rye and 200,000 with winter barley.
Chomiak said cool, moist weather last month would be particularly helpful to barley but might hurt maize.

"Barley should do much better this year than last," he said. "Hectarage was down but there should be higher yields. If the cool weather persists, corn production will not be as good. Corn needs heat."

The government has not provided barley forecasts, but SovEcon Ltd, an independent group studying agriculture production, sees Ukraine's barley output at 7.5 to 8.0 million tonnes against 5.7 million in 1996.
Agriculture Minister Mykhailo Zubets has predicted a "significantly better" maize crop this year compared to last year's 1.8 million tonnes. Ukraine harvested 2.2 million tonnes in 1995.
"I think there will be more cereals produced, definitely an increase over last year," he said earlier.

Chomiak said harvesting had started in the southern peninsula of Crimea, recently hit, as it is every year, by a plague of locusts. But he said the damage could be contained if temperatures cooled and rains increased.
